subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: Heaven as the Upper World
description: A quick win: understand Heaven as the Upper World.

hook.text: Look up. That's where almost every culture placed the divine. Heaven, Olympus, Svarga—gods live above.

buildup.text: The sky is unreachable, vast, and luminous. It provided the perfect metaphor for transcendence.

discovery.text: In Dante's Paradiso, heaven is organized in concentric spheres—each planet a level closer to God.

twist.text: Astronomers proved the sky is empty void. But 'heaven above' still governs religious language and architecture.

climax.text: The upper world is where meaning lives in myth. Even secular people say they 'look up' to someone they admire.

punchline.text: The gods moved. The metaphor stayed.

quiz.question: Why did ancient cultures place the divine in the sky?
options: The sky's vastness and unreachability made it a metaphor for transcendence
